source.title: ÜberWeb: Insights from Multilingual Curation for a 20-Trillion-Token Dataset
source.authors: A. Carranza; Kaleigh Mentzer; R. Monti; Alex Fang; Alvin Deng; Amro Abbas; Anshuman Suri; Brett Larsen; Cody Blakeney; Darren Teh; David Schwab; Diego Kiner; Fan Pan; Haakon Mongstad; Hao-Li Yin; Jack Urbanek; Jason Lee; Jason Telanoff; Josh Wills; Luke Merrick; Maximilian Bother; Parth Doshi; Paul Burstein; Pratyush Maini; Rishabh Adiga; Siddharth Joshi; Spandan Das; T. Jiang; Vineeth Dorna; Zhengping Wang; B. Gaza; Ari S. Morcos; Matthew L. Leavitt

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream performance against training compute in multilingual models, a setting distinct from the original held-out-loss scaling studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports downstream benchmark evaluations and performance-versus-FLOPs comparisons relevant to V6. It does not report held-out cross-entropy loss, fit power laws, predict large-run loss from small runs, or search for compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. The 60B-token curation experiments and their benchmark scores do not test the specified scaling-law versions.
record.test_reason: A data-curation paper. Its compute-axis results (Figure 1, Tables 4–16) compare its own curated 3B/8B models against open-weight baselines trained on different data, to show curation shifts the performance–compute frontier. It fits no power law and reports no held-out loss. It does not test whether downstream performance tracks scale or loss predictably, and it does not vary scale under controlled conditions beyond two model sizes. Scaling laws appear only in related work and in the claim to 'improve on current scaling laws'. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that multilingual regressions ('curse of multilinguality') largely reflect correctable data-quality deficiencies, not capacity limits. In their view, English and non-English curation transfer bidirectionally, and bespoke per-language curation gives the largest gains. Curated 3B/8B models at 1T tokens reach competitive multilingual accuracy with 4–10× fewer FLOPs, establishing a new performance–compute Pareto frontier, and the benefits carry to Trinity Large.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies multilingual data curation and downstream benchmark performance versus FLOPs, rather than fitting held-out cross-entropy scaling laws or finding compute-optimal parameter/token allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that outcomes vary with curation regime, language, and translation-source quality; these are data-curation effects, not sensitivity analyses of scaling-law fits.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched or lower training FLOPs, the curated 3B/8B models (1T tokens, 7.75% multilingual) match or beat open-weight baselines trained with 4–10× more compute on multilingual MMLU, ARC and Belebele. Example: the 3B model at 1.8e22 FLOPs outperforms LFM2.5-1.2B at 1.9e23.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The downstream performance–compute frontier is not fixed by compute alone; data curation and quality can shift it by roughly an order of magnitude in compute.

fits_no_version.finding: In 60B-token bilingual 3B runs, curation of English or non-English data raises downstream scores (3.9%, 1.2% and up to 16.9% relative gains) at fixed model size and tokens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed parameters and tokens, data quality changes downstream multilingual performance substantially.

record.problems: For the relevant compute-performance comparisons, Figure 1 provides plotted values without numerical values in the text, and no uncertainty estimates are reported. The paper does not fit or validate a predictive downstream scaling relationship.
record.rows_left_out: The remaining numerical downstream benchmark results in Tables 4–16 are language-specific and compare models and curation outcomes; they were not extracted because the retained Figure 1 rows capture the study’s reported downstream-performance-versus-compute comparison relevant to V6. The 60B-token curation intervention results are not scaling-law tests.

untested.parts: No held-out loss and no power-law fits.
No power-law fits in other regimes.

No fitted or validated relation between downstream performance and scale or loss. The only within-recipe scale comparison is 3B vs 8B at 1T tokens (8B higher on every table), two points with no predictive test.
No exponent or compute-optimal fits, so no evidence on fit-dependence.

missing.what: Per-language numeric scores for the 3B vs 8B curated models and baselines. These are the only within-recipe size comparison, if anyone wants a two-point downstream-vs-scale datum.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'supports' label is dropped. Beating a compute frontier through better data is not evidence that downstream performance improves predictably with scale. If anything, it bears on data-dependence, but no laws are fitted. FLOPs for baselines are 6ND estimates (Table 3). There are no uncertainty estimates, and the 60B runs use cloze scoring while the 1T runs use MCF.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or power-law fits in parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run loss fits or predictions evaluated against larger runs.
No fixed-compute search for a loss-minimising parameter/token allocation.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
No test of the same power-law form across modalities or training regimes.
The paper compares downstream benchmark results with compute, but does not fit or validate a predictive relationship between downstream performance and scale or pretraining loss.
No analysis of scaling-law exponents, compute-optimal splits, fitting choices, or departures from power-law curves.
